facts.text: Adirondack is a hamlet in Warren County, NY, on Schroon Lake, 32 miles north of Glens Falls.
The Adirondack region spans six million protected acres, the largest natural area in the U.S., with over 100 communities, mountains, lakes, and cliffs.
Lake Placid, near Adirondack, hosted the 1932 and 1980 Winter Olympics, and today offers Mirror Lake paddling and High Peaks hiking.
Fort William Henry, a Revolutionary War landmark, stands in the Adirondack area, echoing 18th-century military history.
The Adirondack Experience museum preserves Great Camps and deep woods, celebrating the region’s rustic heritage.
Summer brings hiking, kayaking, and fishing; winter opens snowmobiling and cross-country skiing across Adirondack’s trails.
